final_recommendation: The room converged on filing an ultra vires petition publicly this week challenging FINMA's retroactive application of Article 36(c), followed by a 72-hour window for FINMA to respond with settlement terms before announcing a recovery floor (35-50 cents). Leverage depends on E&O carriers already being aware of exposure and pushing FINMA toward settlement rather than coordinating a unified defense.
minority_objections: Credit market analyst warned that delaying recovery announcement to file first would let AT1 market confidence continue bleeding
Institutional investor initially pushed for immediate 35-cent announcement today to stabilize market, overruled by counsel on sequencing grounds
key_conflicts: Fundamental disagreement on sequencing: announce recovery floor first (stabilize market) vs. file ultra vires first (preserve leverage)
Dispute over whether E&O carriers would pressure settlement or coordinate unified defense with FINMA
Tension between legal leverage (discovery threat) and market stabilization (public recovery commitment)
key_concessions: FINMA legal conceded the ordinance's retroactive Article 36(c) application is vulnerable to ultra vires challenge
Bondholder group accepted that unilateral 35-cent announcement without FINMA signal would appear as capitulation
All parties acknowledged E&O carriers (Munich Re, Zurich) are already aware of exposure and running tail-risk models
red_lines: No settlement announcement before confirming FINMA's willingness to negotiate recovery percentage
No sealed discovery filing—must be public ultra vires petition to create real settlement pressure
No acceptance of recovery below 35 cents without exhausting litigation leverage first
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Multi-year litigation tail if FINMA refuses settlement and E&O carriers coordinate unified defense
Global AT1 market repricing to whatever interim recovery floor is announced, creating permanent contagion
Director D&O exposure remains unconfirmed—regulatory-act immunity may shield FINMA board entirely
Reinsurance accumulation risk if multiple financial-lines carriers face simultaneous claims across Credit Suisse advisers
downstream_risk_variables: Whether E&O carriers push settlement or coordinate defense after ultra vires filing
FINMA board's actual exposure under regulatory-act immunity doctrine
Market reaction to 72-hour settlement window vs. immediate recovery announcement
Duration and severity of AT1 issuance freeze while litigation proceeds
Scope of discovery naming external counsel as custodians and its impact on insurer defense costs
uncertainty_notes: Critical uncertainty: whether FINMA's E&O carriers will pressure settlement (as institutional investor claims based on Munich Re/Zurich signals) or coordinate unified defense with FINMA's outside counsel. The room also left unresolved whether FINMA directors face personal D&O liability or are fully shielded, which determines the real settlement lever. Final sequencing (file then announce vs. announce then file) was decided but remains vulnerable to market-confidence collapse during the 72-hour window.

marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: Article 36(c) retroactive application challenge was the spine of the entire strategy; FINMA legal conceded ordinance vulnerability; bondholder counsel built detailed ultra vires case
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Mentioned as precedent concern and market repricing driver, but not the central lever—litigation focused on ordinance validity, not hierarchy inversion itself
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 market bleeding and repricing discussed throughout, but subordinated to litigation sequencing debates; treated as consequence, not driver
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Multi-year litigation tail acknowledged but not developed as structured risk; room focused on forcing settlement within 72 hours, not modeling tail duration/severity
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: E&O carrier exposure (Munich Re, Zurich) and settlement pressure became the decisive lever in final rounds; institutional investor's insurer intelligence drove convergence on filing sequence
